title: Right-side trunk EMG (%MVC) at peak isometric axial torque, pre-rotation -30°, ccw effort
condition: maximal isometric axial twist ccw, trunk pre-rotated -30°, standing, pelvis fixed

quantity.name: normalised EMG at peak axial torque
quantity.definition: Linear envelope (full-wave rectified, 3 Hz low-pass) normalised to the maximum activity of that site over 4 MVC strategies, 3 trials each: restrained bent-knee sit-up; 'hanging' over the table edge (supine flexion, side-lying lateral bend, prone extension against resistance); standing flexion/lateral bend/extension against a chest strap with pelvis fixed; maximal isometric twists (if higher). Lower ES max always from prone 'hang-extend'; RA mostly 'hang-flex' (Table 2).

source.n: 15 subjects in Table 3 (10 M, 5 F); 11 M + 5 F in MVC-normalisation part
source.sample: healthy university students, no LBP for >=1 year, in vivo

protocol.summary: Standing; pelvis fixed (ASIS rigid fixator + adjustable belt); upper-torso jig harness clamped at shoulder level (handles for arm position) connected through a ~0.6 m telescopic shaft with two universal joints to a Cybex II head mounted overhead with vertical axle: trunk free in all directions except axial rotation, so only axial torque about the vertical dynamometer axis is measured (no coupled moments recorded). 3 trials per condition, slow build-up to peak at ~4 s. Six bipolar Ag-AgCl surface electrode pairs on the right side only; 10-500 Hz, 1000 Hz sampling.
how_to_simulate: Simulate the twist as in mcgill1991.axial_torque_minus30deg_ccw_<sex> (standing, pelvis fixed, pre-rotation -30°, torque = measured mean).
Normalise model muscle activation by each muscle's maximum over simulated flexion, extension, lateral bend and twist MVCs (or by PCSA x max stress).
Compare right-side activations under the six sites (RA, EO ~15 cm, IO, latissimus at T9, ES 5 cm at T9, ES 3 cm at L3).
protocol.notes: Direction naming: cw/ccw as printed. From the right-side muscle pattern (right IO and latissimus agonists in cw, right EO agonist in ccw), cw corresponds to twisting the trunk to the right (right axial rotation) - inferred, not stated. '+30°' = trunk pre-rotated in the cw direction (Table 3 footnote). Activations are far below 100% even at maximal twist (author's model with these EMGs underpredicted 91 Nm as 14 Nm).
